theme: Country-level Airbnb studies with shared data: OECD/EU/UN reports with data appendices on platform tourism, Eurostat-Airbnb data-sharing agreement outputs, ECB/IMF papers
queries_run: gh search repos: eurostat tourism platform
gh search repos: oecd platform economy tourism
gh search repos: collaborative economy airbnb
gh search repos: sharing economy Eurostat
gh search repos: short-term rental Europe data
gh search repos: imf tourism statistics
gh search repos: pandasdmx / sdmx1 statistical data
gh search repos: eurostat python client
gh search repos: OECD data R package
gh search repos: eurostat (top by stars)
gh search repos: OECD API python
WebSearch site:github.com eurostat airbnb data sharing platform accommodation (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)
WebSearch site:github.com OECD platform tourism statistics data (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)

candidates.name: rOpenGov/eurostat
candidates.what_it_holds: CRAN R package (255 stars, active, updated 14 Sep 2026) that queries the full Eurostat bulk/SDMX API and returns tidy data frames, including the tour_ce_omr collaborative-economy-nights table already held, but also every other Eurostat tourism table (tour_occ_arn/tour_occ_nim occupancy, tour_dem_ttw demand) at NUTS2 regional granularity, not just country level. Also fetches dataset release/vintage metadata.
candidates.why_useful: Same underlying data as our held tour_ce_omr series but a one-call method to also pull sub-national (NUTS2) EU tourism/accommodation series and vintage/revision metadata -- addresses gap 4 (point-in-time macro vintages) and could give EMEA regional granularity finer than what we hold.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: tour_ce_omr country-level series already held; this is a broader/finer-grained acquisition method for the same family
candidates.time_coverage: Eurostat coverage, typically 2000s-present depending on table
candidates.size_hint: API client, no bundled data files

candidates.name: eurostat/restatapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat-org R package (35 stars, updated Jul 2026) to search and retrieve any Eurostat dataset via SDMX, maintained by Eurostat itself.
candidates.why_useful: Official first-party alternative to rOpenGov/eurostat for pulling tour_ce_omr and related platform-tourism tables with guaranteed schema stability; useful if the community package lags a Eurostat table change.

candidates.name: eurostat/pyrostat
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat-org Python API/CLI for searching and bulk-downloading Eurostat data collections (SDMX/JSON-stat/bulk TSV), Python equivalent of restatapi.
candidates.why_useful: Python-native (matches repo's pandas/duckdb stack) route to the same Eurostat platform-tourism and accommodation tables, and to non-tourism Eurostat series (HICP, consumer confidence) already partly held from other sources.

candidates.name: ondata/opensdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: Python CLI and library (52 stars, updated 14 Sep 2026, MIT) that speaks SDMX 2.1 REST against ANY compliant statistical-agency API -- explicitly lists Eurostat, ISTAT, OECD, ECB, and World Bank as supported endpoints, with an 'AI-ready' structured output mode.
candidates.why_useful: A single generic tool that reaches the whole theme's target agencies (Eurostat platform nights, OECD tourism/consumer-confidence tables, ECB statistical series for FX/rates papers) without needing a separate client per agency -- directly useful for pulling OECD platform-economy or tourism satellite-account tables and ECB series referenced in ECB working papers on the sharing economy.
candidates.geography: EU, OECD member states (global coverage via OECD/World Bank)
candidates.time_coverage: whatever each source SDMX endpoint covers

candidates.name: ahuarte47/duckdb-eurostat
candidates.what_it_holds: DuckDB extension (35 stars, MIT, updated 9 Sep 2026) that exposes the Eurostat database as SQL tables directly inside DuckDB, so any Eurostat dataset (including tour_ce_omr and related tourism/accommodation tables) can be queried with plain SQL.
candidates.why_useful: Repo's own environment already uses DuckDB for large-store queries; this extension would let the team pull/refresh Eurostat platform-tourism tables in the same DuckDB workflow used for Inside Airbnb, with no separate Python/R dependency.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same Eurostat tables already held via other means
candidates.size_hint: extension binary + SQL macros, no bundled data

candidates.name: hanlulong/openecon-data
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server + web UI (71 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026) aggregating ~330K macro/economic indicators across FRED, World Bank, IMF, and Eurostat into one queryable interface for AI agents.
candidates.why_useful: One integration point that reaches IMF's tourism/travel-services balance-of-payments series and Eurostat tables together -- could shortcut building separate IMF and Eurostat pulls for the country-level travel-demand and platform-tourism gaps (7, 6).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: FRED portion already held; IMF/Eurostat portions are new access methods only
candidates.size_hint: MCP server code, no bundled dataset

candidates.name: eurostat/statistics-coded
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat-org catalogue (41 stars) of R/Python/SQL/SAS/Stata code snippets that reproduce the charts/tables behind Eurostat 'Statistics Explained' articles -- some of these articles cover tourism, the collaborative economy, and short-stay accommodation.
candidates.why_useful: If any Statistics Explained article on platform/collaborative-economy tourism has reproducible code here, it gives a documented, exact recipe for rebuilding the Eurostat-Airbnb data-sharing-agreement output tables (tour_ce_omr and siblings) rather than reverse-engineering the API from scratch.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: points to the same tour_ce_omr family already held

candidates.name: opus-42/eurostat-api-client
candidates.what_it_holds: Small, simple Python client (7 stars, updated 20 Mar 2026, Apache-2.0) to query the Eurostat REST API; minimal feature set compared to pyrostat/restatapi.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight fallback Eurostat client if the official packages are too heavy; marginal incremental value over rOpenGov/eurostat and pyrostat above.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same Eurostat tables already held; strictly dominated by pyrostat/restatapi

notes: Direct hits are essentially zero: no repo on GitHub packages the actual Eurostat-Airbnb data-sharing-agreement outputs, an OECD platform-tourism report's data appendix, or an ECB/IMF working-paper replication package on short-term rentals/the sharing economy -- these reports circulate as PDFs with tables, not as GitHub datasets, and the underlying series (tour_ce_omr) is already held. What GitHub does offer for this theme is exclusively ACQUISITION METHOD tooling: official and community SDMX/REST clients (Eurostat's own pyrostat/restatapi, rOpenGov/eurostat, the generic multi-agency ondata/opensdmx which also reaches OECD and ECB, and a DuckDB extension) that make it easy to pull Eurostat tourism/accommodation tables (and, via opensdmx/openecon-data, OECD and IMF series) beyond the single tour_ce_omr series already captured -- e.g., NUTS2 regional breakdowns or occupancy/demand companion tables. No IMF-specific client or IMF tourism/travel-BoP dataset repo was found; that remains an open thread given search-budget limits (gh search repos was rate-limited mid-run at 403, and WebSearch had already exhausted its 200-query session budget before this scout could run any query, so no site:github.com fallback was available -- a future scout with fresh WebSearch budget should retry 'site:github.com IMF tourism travel services data', 'ECB working paper sharing economy replication github', and 'OECD.Stat SDMX python client' directly). Recommend a human check whether Eurostat's own site (not GitHub) publishes a downloadable data appendix for the original Airbnb-Eurostat data-sharing-agreement press release, since that would be a non-GitHub but still free/point-in-time source worth a separate scout.
